question: How did criterion 2 get its final form?

revisions.statement: Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer
Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer

revisions.threshold: control's max balanced accuracy over layers does not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings
revisions.note: A leak bound, not a selectivity floor: under a type-disjoint split the control task's ceiling is chance. Drafted as 0.50 ± 0.03 (b9c861b); replaced before the push because ±0.03 fires 59–80% of the time with no leak (61bf29e).

answer:
Criterion 2 went through three registered revisions.

1. **Revision 1** (commit 12a0349, 2026-08-22) set it as a selectivity floor. Selectivity (real minus control) at the best layer had to be ≥ 0.10 [crit-rev1-2].

2. **Revision 2** (commit c7323d0, same day) kept the same statement but marked the 0.10 threshold as "provisional." It supersedes revision 1 [crit-rev2-2]. The rows don't say why it was flagged provisional.

3. **Revision 3** (commit cb09c9d, 2026-09-26) is the current form and supersedes revision 2. It changed the criterion from a selectivity floor to a leak bound called "Control task shows no leak." The control task's maximum balanced accuracy over layers must not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings [crit-rev3-2]. The stated reason is that under a type-disjoint split, the control task's ceiling is chance [crit-rev3-2]. The revision cites Hewitt & Liang 2019, §2.3 [paper-hewitt-liang].

Before revision 3 was pushed, an intermediate draft set the bound as 0.50 ± 0.03 (b9c861b). That draft was replaced (61bf29e) because a ±0.03 band would fire 59–80% of the time even with no leak [crit-rev3-2]. The permutation-based 95th-percentile threshold took its place.
